The computational resource we will use for this course is the OU Supercomputing Center for Education and Research ([OSCER](https://www.ou.edu/oscer)). 

# OSCER Account Creation and Management

## Signing Up for an Account

Anyone on a project where the instructor, or at least one Principal or Co-Principal Investigator, is a faculty or staff member at an Oklahoma institution is eligible for an account.

Please visit the following link, which will take you to the page to sign up for an account: [ACCOUNT SIGN UP](https://www.ou.edu/oscer/getting-started/new-account)

Follow step one and wait for confirmation of approval for your account before proceeding to steps 2-3. When asked for a PI and group in the application, please put **Eleana Cabello** and **okinbreclass**.

## Changing or Forgetting Password

If you forget your password, please visit the following link and follow the steps outlined: [CHANGE PASSWORD](https://www.ou.edu/oscer/getting-started/change-password)

# Accessing OSCER Account

## Logging on using MobaXterm - Windows

If you have a Windows system, please follow the steps on OSCER’s page to install MobaXterm, linked here under the Windows (a) MobaxTerm section: [OSCER's Getting Started Page](https://www.ou.edu/oscer/getting-started/machine-access#mobaxterm)

Once the terminal window appears, please enter your credentials correctly. You will see a wall of text with OSCER info, and finally at the end a line indicating you are logged on to an OSCER login node: `(base) [USER@sooner# ~]$`

## Logging on through Terminal - MacOS and Linux

If you have a Mac or Linux system, to log into OSCER, please have your username and password on hand. On your computer, open up the terminal application. Once on the terminal, please type in: `ssh USERNAME@sooner.oscer.ou.edu` 

Afterwards, it will prompt you to type in your password. Start typing it in. Do not worry if it does not appear on the screen when you are typing, it is normal. After you have typed it in, click your Enter key.

If you entered your credentials correctly, you will see a wall of text with OSCER info, and finally, at the end, a line indicating you are logged on to an OSCER login node: `(base) [USER@sooner# ~]$`

At the end of this process, you should be logged into a sooner login node on OSCER!
